answer.justification: The recurrent laryngeal nerve runs in close proximity to the inferior thyroid artery within the tracheoesophageal groove. Ligation of the inferior thyroid artery, especially when performed close to the thyroid gland, significantly increases the risk of injuring the recurrent laryngeal nerve. Damage to this nerve leads to paralysis of the intrinsic muscles of the larynx (except the cricothyroid), resulting in the clinical presentation of hoarseness.
